_comment: Carbon and Its Compounds WS1 — no printed key; answers DERIVED (merged A+B).

2.reason: Isomers share molecular formula (2 true) and propane C3H8 has no isomers (4 true); not structural formula nor chemical properties.

4.reason: A covalent bond between two identical non-metals shares the electron pair equally.

6.reason: C3H8, CH4, C2H6 are alkanes (CnH2n+2); C4H8 is an alkene, different series.

7.reason: C2H6, C4H10, C5H12 are alkanes; C7H14 is an alkene (CnH2n), the odd one out.

9.reason: Ethyne H-C#C-H: triple bond shares 6 electrons + two C-H bonds share 4 = 10 total.

10.reason: Glacial acetic acid freezes at 16.6 C, so it is solid (not liquid) at 10 C.

11.reason: Only esterification (II) gives a product (ester) with more carbon atoms than the underlined alcohol; oxidation keeps C the same, and the others lose carbon.

13.reason: Fluorine is an element, not an allotrope of carbon; diamond, graphite, fullerene are.

14.reason: C2H6O used to sterilise skin = ethanol (C2H5OH); oxidation gives acetic acid CH3COOH, same 2 carbons.

16.reason: Conc. H2SO4 in esterification acts as a dehydrating agent; the process is esterification.

17.reason: Addition reactions need unsaturation: C3H6 (propene) and C2H2 (ethyne); the others are saturated/alcohol.

18.reason: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-C#CH is a 6-carbon chain with a terminal triple bond = hex-1-yne.

19.reason: REVIEW: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are all true and statement 2 (aldehyde/carboxyl non-terminal) is false; both option A (I,III) and option B (III,IV) contain only true statements, so the question is ambiguous. Chose A as statement 1 is foundational.

20.reason: Forming 4 bonds gives carbon 8 valence electrons = neon configuration.

21.reason: -OH present in propanol (2) and ethanol (4) = 'B and D' per the worksheet's letter labels for statements 2 and 4.

22.reason: CH3CH2-COOCH3 is methyl propanoate, not 'Ethanoic acid', so the IUPAC name given is incorrect.

23.reason: Ethanol vapour in breath causes a chemical (redox colour) change that the analyzer detects.

25.reason: Buckminsterfullerene (C60) is an allotrope of carbon.

26.reason: Magnesium sulphate (ii) and calcium chloride (iii) introduce Mg2+/Ca2+ causing hardness; the sodium salts do not.

27.reason: Chlorine substitutes saturated hydrocarbons at room temperature only in the presence of sunlight.

28.reason: Mineral acids are stronger because they are completely ionised (i) while carboxylic acids are only partially ionised (iv).

29.reason: Saponification = ester + NaOH -> sodium salt + alcohol (CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + C2H5OH).

30.reason: HCOO-CH2CH2CH3 (propyl methanoate) is formed from formic acid and propanol.

31.reason: Soft soaps are the potassium salts of fatty acids.

32.reason: CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3 is a 4-carbon chain with a methyl on C2 = 2-methylbutane.

33.reason: -COOH is the carboxyl group of carboxylic acids.

34.reason: Successive homologues differ by CH2 = 12 + 2 = 14 amu.

35.reason: Butanone is a ketone with the -CO- functional group.

36.reason: Ethanol C2H5OH contains two carbon atoms.

38.reason: Kekule benzene C6H6 has 3 C=C double bonds and 3 C-C + 6 C-H = 9 single bonds; 9 and 3.

39.reason: Unsaturated = (ii) alkyne C#C and (iv) alkene C=C; (i) and (iii) are saturated alkanes.

40.reason: CH2=CH2 + Br2 -> BrCH2-CH2Br adds across the double bond = addition reaction.

41.reason: Ethyne (acetylene) gives the very hot oxy-acetylene flame used to weld/cut metals; ethane and ethene are not.

42.reason: Activated charcoal adsorbs coloured impurities, so it is used as a decolourizing agent in the sugar industry.

43.reason: Hydrogenation of oils to fats adds H2 across the C=C double bond over Ni/Pd — an addition reaction.

44.reason: A soap molecule has a polar/ionic hydrophilic head (-COO-Na+) and a long non-polar hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail.

45.reason: REVIEW: Smaller-chain acid (X, ~C11) has the lower melting point and is the more liquid-like of the two; the C20 acid Y is a solid. (X = undecanoic acid mp ~28-29C is borderline solid at 25C, but X is the intended answer as the lower-melting one.)

47.reason: Esters such as ethyl ethanoate (CH3COOC2H5) give fruits their characteristic sweet smell.

48.reason: CH3CH2COOH (propanoic acid) carries the carboxylic -COOH group; the others are alkane, ester and alcohol.

50.reason: Ethyne is H-C(triple bond)C-H; option C (H3-) is invalid and B/D are ethene/ethane.

52.reason: Both true: adjacent homologues differ by CH2 = 14 u, and a homologous series shares elements + functional group. But S2 (same functional group) does not explain the 14 u mass difference (that is due to the -CH2- unit), so S2 is not the correct explanation of S1.

54.reason: In a micelle the ionic/hydrophilic heads face out into the water (surface) while the hydrophobic carbon chains point into the interior.

55.reason: Carbon is present in the atmosphere chiefly as carbon dioxide. (Standard NCERT answer: CO2 only.)

56.reason: Catenation, tetravalency and (consequent) isomerism enable carbon's huge number of compounds; allotropy (forms of the element itself) is not responsible for compound formation.

57.reason: Pencil 'lead' is graphite (mixed with clay), not the element lead.

59.reason: Fermentation is anaerobic (needs absence of air), needs no light and only a moderate temperature, so none of presence-of-air/light/very-high-temperature is favourable -> None of these.

60.reason: Heteroatoms are non-C/H atoms; in CH3-CH2-O-CH2-CH2Cl these are oxygen (i) and chlorine (iv).

61.reason: Ammonia has three N-H single covalent bonds only.

63.reason: Saponification = ester + NaOH -> salt (soap) + alcohol: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + C2H5OH.

64.reason: Ethanol -> ethanoic acid with acidified K2Cr2O7 is an OXIDATION, not combustion; so option A is named incorrectly.

65.reason: False statements are 1 and 2: both soaps and detergents are water soluble (1 false); soaps ARE biodegradable while many detergents are not (2 reverses reality, false). Statements 3 and 4 are true.

66.reason: Ethanol is commonly called ethyl alcohol.

67.reason: Hardness is caused by dissolved Ca/Mg salts — Mg(HCO3)2, CaCl2 and CaSO4 all contribute, so 'All of these'.

68.reason: Organic compounds generally have LOW melting and boiling points (covalent, weak intermolecular forces); the high-mp/bp claim is not true.

69.reason: Alcohol burns with a clean non-luminous (blue) flame due to complete combustion.

71.reason: Statements 1 (differ by -CH2) and 2 (mp/bp rise with molecular mass) are true. 3 is false (successive members differ by 14 u, not 16). 4 is false: alkynes CnH(2n-2) include C2H2 (ethyne) and C3H4 (propyne) which ARE successive members. So correct = (a) and (b).

72.reason: CH3-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3 is a 4-carbon chain with -OH on C2 = butan-2-ol (2-butanol).

73.reason: Only option D gives two C3H6O2 isomers: propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH, -COOH) and methyl ethanoate (CH3COOCH3, ester -COOR). The aldehyde/ketone options are C3H6O, not C3H6O2.

74.reason: Pentane C5H12: 4 C-C bonds + 12 C-H bonds = 16 covalent bonds.

75.reason: Ethanol + Na -> sodium ethoxide (C2H5ONa) + hydrogen gas.

1.reason: A is cyclohexane (each C has 2 H, all single bonds — saturated); B is benzene and C is a cyclohexadiene, both unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbons.

15.reason: A (n-hexane), B (2-methylpentane) and D (2,3-dimethylbutane) each have 6 carbons = C6H14; C is neopentane (central C bonded to 4 CH3) = 5 carbons = C5H12.

24.reason: In H2O oxygen forms two shared electron pairs (one with each H) and keeps two lone pairs; only option c shows both O-H bonds as shared pairs plus two lone pairs on O.

49.reason: Butanoic acid is CH3-CH2-CH2-COOH: a 4-carbon chain ending in a carbonyl C double-bonded to O and bonded to OH; only option a shows 4 carbons with the terminal C=O and -OH.

70.reason: Cyclohexane (C6H12) is a saturated 6-membered ring with all single bonds and a CH2 at each vertex; only option b has no double or triple bonds.
